title: The Old Roof
logline: Every few years a family strips the old palm leaves off their roof and weaves on new ones, and by their own account it is still the same roof, though no single leaf on it is the one that was there before.

object.note: Object 9 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: A festival frame that stands only because nothing in it stands alone becomes a roof renewed leaf by leaf, still 'the same roof' each year, an echo of 'The Same Boat'.

thread_out.thread: Roofs carry across: from palm thatch in the dry south to estate homes through a hard monsoon, where rain and cold change how neighbours keep company.

requirements: A household that still re-thatches or renews part of its home by hand
A renewal that can realistically be completed within the filming window
Willingness to discuss whether they would prefer a different roof

suggestions.name: A coastal home where palm-thatch roofing is still practised
suggestions.region: Southern Province, Hambantota or Tangalle area
suggestions.why: Traditional palm-thatch roofing survives in pockets of the southern coast alongside more modern roofing.
suggestions.verify: A specific household still re-thatching by hand must be found and confirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: A roof can be 'the same roof' for years even though every leaf on it has been replaced. The texts describe a life in a similar way: not exactly the same as before, not something else, with nothing carried across.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: වහලේ සෑම අත්තක්ම අලුත් වුවත් එය 'අපේ පරණ වහලයම' වන්නාක් මෙන්, ජීවිතයක පැවැත්ම ද හරියටම එකම දෙයක්වත් වෙනම දෙයක්වත් නොවන අතර, එක් තැනකින් අනෙක් තැනට කිසිවක් ගමන් නොකරයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Pradeepika gives four ways of seeing the chain. The method of identity sees an unbroken continuity, like a seed becoming sprout, leaf, trunk and branch; the method of diversity sees each link as new and distinct; each one, seen rightly, removes one wrong view, and misread, produces another. The texts also say nothing comes over from an earlier life, yet nothing appears without a cause: if the two were simply the same, curd could not come from milk, and if they were simply different, curd would have nothing to do with milk. A skill learned as a child lives on in the adult's hands and goes to no one else.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Old, blackened leaf is stripped away until the bare frame shows, and new green leaf is woven on by old and young together. The family speaks plainly about a roof that is always changing and always theirs, and the viewer can hold both at once: nothing old is carried over, yet the new roof exists only because of the old.

key_terms.en: the method of diversity (each link distinct)

lesson.caution: It does not mean a soul moves from one life to the next: the texts reject exactly that view, and the roof is only an everyday picture of continuity without a traveller.
lesson.builds_on: The leaning poles showed things holding each other up at one moment; the roof carries that across time, showing a continuity made entirely of new parts.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
